reply:
What P@x sends to Anthropic

To do what you ask, P@x sends these to Anthropic over an encrypted connection:
- what you ask, as text;
- pictures of the window P@x is working in, or of the screen when a task needs it;
- the names and states of buttons and other controls in that window;
- the results of the tools and commands P@x runs for you;
- the things P@x remembers that matter to the task.

Never sent:
- the sound of your voice (speech is turned into text on this computer);
- the trusted screen, sign-in prompts and password managers;
- windows of applications you exclude;
- passwords and keys stored by the system;
- support bundles, unless you attach one yourself.

In this version
P@x cannot see or use the screen yet, so no pictures and no names of controls are sent. It uses TUR's own tools and commands that only read.

Reminders and scheduled tasks
A scheduled task runs when you may not be there, also while the screen is locked. It can look things up and make changes that can be undone. What it reads is sent to Anthropic like the results of any other task. Anything else it would need waits for you.

Memory
Memory stays on this computer. When something P@x remembers matters to a task, it is sent to Anthropic with that task. That includes things P@x read somewhere and you chose to keep: they are sent again whenever they matter.

Other programs
On this desktop, any program you run can see your screen and use the keyboard and pointer. TUR limits what P@x may do. It cannot limit other programs you start.

What Anthropic keeps
P@x asks every provider not to store your conversations where the provider offers that choice. P@x sends Anthropic the whole conversation with each request. The interface P@x uses has no setting for storing a conversation, so there is nothing for P@x to switch off.
Anthropic's terms are not reviewed by TUR: TUR has not read what Anthropic keeps, for how long, whether it trains on it, or where it processes it. Read them before you go on.
What Anthropic keeps anyway, and for how long, is governed by Anthropic's terms, not by TUR. TUR cannot control it.
Anthropic's data terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms

You can see everything P@x did in Settings ▸ P@x ▸ Activity, and stop P@x at any time.

reply.note: SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-TUR-Noncommercial-1.0.0. An EXAMPLE, not a maintained price list. Model names and prices were read on 2026-11-12 from each provider's own pricing page (prices_url) and are the standard, pay-as-you-go prices in USD per million tokens. Each provider changes them without notice. Where a provider charges by prompt length, the price for the shortest prompts is given, which is what a task of P@x normally sends: Anthropic none; OpenAI up to 272K input tokens; Google none for the models listed. A model listed without prices has a price this format cannot state truthfully: tiered by prompt length (claude-haiku-5-5), or announced to change within weeks (gemini-4-carbon, from 2026-12-01). P@x then limits it in tokens. max_output_tokens is P@x's own limit for one response, chosen to bound what one response can cost; it is not the provider's maximum. No model here has been run with TUR: tested_with_tur is false everywhere. Each provider is an identifier with an adapter family (ADR-0004, amended 2026-11-12). The presets of the OpenAI-compatible family (adapter openai-chat) were read from each service's own documentation on 2026-11-12; the pages are in docs/architecture/pax-providers.md, section 14. Their prices are EXAMPLES too: DeepSeek's are its peak rates (off-peak rates are half; peak is 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC on weekdays), and its page shows them in dollars without naming the currency; xAI's and Mistral's are for prompts under 200K tokens where the page tiers them. Context sizes are as the pages write them (1M read as 1000000, 256k as 256000). capabilities are what the pages declare, not what TUR measured. data_terms are TUR's summary of the pages named in sources, read on reviewed_on; the three companies' entries have none, so their consent text says their terms are not reviewed by TUR. The two local presets point at the standard addresses of Ollama (127.0.0.1:11434) and llama.cpp's llama-server (127.0.0.1:9931), take no key, and declare nothing about tools: that depends on the model and on how the server was started. The preset local is TUR's own local AI, tur-ai-local (docs/architecture/local-ai.md): its address 127.0.0.1:39281, its key read from the file tur-ai-local writes in the session's runtime directory each time it starts a model (runtime_key_file, never the password store), and its models the chat models of its catalogue that call tools, with the context size it serves (8192 tokens) and an output limit of 1024 tokens chosen by P@x.
